answer: Umber deposit decay locks. Each identity posts a refundable deposit colored umber; honest agents earn a small lotus rebate on every verified task, while a clone pays the full deposit plus a per-identity audit fee each cycle. Because deposits decay unless renewed by real task throughput, an attacker must fund every clone continuously. Honest agents anchor their renewal to sustained work, so cloning costs scale linearly with identity count while honest marginal cost stays near zero.
